prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (non-exhaustive)

Health and care
- Reduce waiting times by recruiting 27,500 nurses, 4,600 doctors, 10,250 allied health professionals; add 10,000 hospital beds; raise pay for lowest‑paid NHS staff by about £1,000 a year.
- Prioritise prevention: restore free dental and eye checks; expand scanning/diagnostics; expand public‑health coordination.
- Provide free personal care for those with long‑term needs.
- Create Patient Care Guarantees; expand mental health and social care capacity; end mixed wards; ban age discrimination in care.
- Establish a Pharmaceutical Agency to end regional drug “postcode lotteries”; move toward reducing, then scrapping, prescription charges.
- Cut central bureaucracy; strengthen local accountability; introduce no‑fault compensation.
- Environmental health measures on home energy efficiency and air quality.

Education, skills and jobs
- Funded by +1p on basic income tax: cut primary class sizes to an average of 25; recruit 5,000 secondary teachers; add classroom assistants; paid preparation time; training salaries for trainees; increase books/ICT.
- Replace national curriculum with a Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; reduce testing at age 7; reform inspections.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for poorer students; raise loan repayment threshold; improve staff pay equity.
- Lifelong learning entitlements (to Level 2 for adults; to Level 3 for 16–24s); merge funding bodies; paid study leave for 16–24s; SME training incentives; replace existing job schemes with a flexible, unified jobs/benefits service.

Law, order and justice
- Recruit 6,000 additional police; 2,000 part‑time retained community officers; form a Community Safety Force; create an independent police complaints system.
- Expand victims’ rights (impact statements); establish hate‑crime units; retain jury trial for mid‑level offences; end most mandatory sentencing.
- Shift from warehousing to rehabilitation: work, skills and resettlement plans in prisons; greater use of effective community sentences; restorative youth justice.

Transport
- Free off‑peak local bus travel for pensioners and disabled people; aim for half‑price fares for under‑19s in full‑time education.
- Greener vehicle taxes (zero VED for the cleanest); no real‑terms rise in fuel duty this Parliament.
- Empower councils to use bonds, congestion charging and parking levies to fund public transport; re‑open lines/stations; rural transport fund.
- Create a Sustainable Transport Authority; increase public‑interest control of rail; restructure rail infrastructure; implement safety reforms.
- Keep air traffic control not‑for‑profit; tighten night‑flight controls; pursue aviation fuel tax reform internationally.

Pensions, incomes and benefits
- Raise the basic state pension with larger uplifts for over‑75s and over‑80s; form an Independent Pensions Authority.
- Long‑term: personal second‑pension accounts; extend basic pension eligibility to all citizens.
- Review the minimum wage annually and apply a single rate from age 16.
- Extra support for children in long‑term low‑income households; reform child maintenance via family courts; extend winter fuel support to the severely disabled; reduce tax burden on the lowest paid over time.

Economy, tax, business and work
- Finance priorities via a 50% income tax rate above £100,000 and Capital Gains Tax reforms; publish a Citizen’s Tax Contract and an annual Fiscal Assessment.
- Enable euro entry subject to a referendum; strengthen Bank of England independence; allow devolved/regional/local borrowing for investment.
- Establish a Green Tax Commission; replace the Climate Change Levy with a carbon tax; target 10% renewable electricity by 2010, rising thereafter; phase out nuclear as stations retire.
- Cut red tape (sunset clauses); £1,500 small‑business rates allowance; promote mutuals/employee ownership; expand public research.
- Toughen competition policy and bank regulation; universal Post Office network obligation.
- Strengthen health and safety enforcement; ban compulsory retirement ages; require consultation on major workplace decisions.

Governance, rights and communities
- Referendum on Westminster voting reform; STV for local/European elections; votes and candidacy from age 16; replace the Lords with an elected Senate; strengthen select committees; Civil Service Act.
- Further devolution; regional assemblies by referendum; replace Council Tax with local income tax.
- Equality Act and commission; stronger Freedom of Information; judicial warrants for surveillance; oppose ID cards; faster, fairer asylum processing and support; civil partnerships; animal welfare commission.
- Community regeneration via a one‑stop grant; doorstep recycling nationwide; flood‑risk reforms; marine protected areas; CAP/CFP reform; Ministry for Rural Affairs.
- Housing and planning: brownfield first; boost affordability and tenants’/leaseholders’ rights; require planning permission for mobile masts.

Europe, foreign policy, defence and development
- EU constitutional clarity, transparency and subsidiarity; enlargement; limited veto retention; single European Parliament seat; stronger UK scrutiny.
- End subsidies for arms exports; strengthen the UN, ICC and peacekeeping; maintain defence spending with flexible, deployable forces; retain a minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing disarmament; oppose national missile defence; moratorium on depleted uranium.
- Raise aid to 0.7% GNI; untie aid; integrate environment into WTO rules; promote universal primary education; expand HIV/AIDS action; enforce anti‑bribery rules.
